subject: How to estimate overlapping corners in equal spaced zigzag distance sampling

messages.author: fa09ce1b52764334
messages.subject: How to estimate overlapping corners in equal spaced zigzag distance sampling
parts:
Dear collegues,

I am a bit stuck in an analytical procedure and maybe you could provide me some light…

I have a zigzag equally spaced survey and would like to apply a correction for overlapping corners where two transects meet (areas surveyed twice). I would like to apply a correction to the total coverage area to account for the double-counting effort and avoid potential bias. I have seen in a previous analysis that you can add it as multiplier called “overlap” within Distance software, for example, but I dont know how to estimate the number that goes in there. I guess I should entre my shape file or coordinates with the tracks/transects somewhere first and define my truncation distance. I also use R, so if you think it´s easier with a package function.

Thanks a lot in advance!

Daniel

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] How to estimate overlapping corners in equal spaced zigzag distance sampling
parts:
Daniel

I am not acquainted with analyses that have used a multiplier for zigzag surveys to address overlapping coverage at the end of transects. Depending upon the size of your study area, I would expect this area to be small. Compound the small size of overlap with a detection probability <1, implying the likelihood of double-counting is pretty small. I would think this would be a second- or third-order problem for your analysis. Maybe I'm wrong, but I would think this area of overlap would be <5% for many study areas. Double counting is seldom a first-order problem in distance sampling surveys unless animals are being "driven" from one transect to the next. Good field procedures can further minimise the issue.

See slide 6 of this online lecture:
https://workshops.distancesampling.org/online-course/lecturepdfs/Ch2/L2-3%20Making%20Distance%20Sampling%20Work.pdf

I guess that if I deal with the double-counting observation at corners (driven then just to one of the lines), not taking into account the overlap areas would not introduce significant bias to the results being small %...

Thanks a lot,
Daniel
